dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?

Hello, yes. My name is Yuki Mensah, and I'm calling about a drain. First, it's frozen shut. Second, there's water spreading across the whole intersection. And third, nobody seems to have looked at it, and it's been like this for days.
Okay, Ms. Mensah, let me get that down. Where is the intersection?
I'm at 24 Ruggles Avenue, up on the Hill. The drain is at the corner right by my house, where Ruggles meets the cross street.
24 Ruggles Avenue. And the grate on the corner is frozen over, you said?

Frozen solid. There's a sheet of ice sitting right on top of the grate. And here's the thing, it hasn't rained. It hasn't snowed either. There's no storm. It's just dry weather and water keeps coming down the street from somewhere, and it has nowhere to go, so it spreads across the intersection and freezes at night.
So it's a steady trickle, not runoff from weather. Do you know where the water is coming from? A broken main, maybe, or a hydrant?

I don't know. First, I haven't seen any hydrant leaking. Second, it seems to start up the block. Third, it runs down along the curb and pools at the drain. It's running right now, in the middle of the day, so it's not just melt.
Alright. That's helpful. It's running now, midday, Friday, and pooling at the corner drain. Is the ice thick enough that people are slipping?

Yes. The mail carrier almost went down on Wednesday. Also, one more thing. There's a manhole cover in that same intersection that looks off. It sits maybe an inch high on one side. Cars hit it and it clunks.
A manhole cover sitting about an inch off. Is it in the same spot as the water, or a bit away from it?
About ten feet from the drain, toward the middle of the intersection. I can't say if the two things are connected. I'm not an engineer. I just know the water goes right past it.

Understood. I'll note both, the frozen grate and the cover. Let me say it back so I have it right. Twenty-four Ruggles Avenue, Historic Hill, corner drain iced over, water running in dry weather and spreading across the intersection, and a manhole cover about an inch off nearby.
That's right. Now, can I ask something? First, is this a city drain or a state one? Because somebody told me some of the roads up here belong to the state, and I don't want to be sent in a circle.

Good question. Ruggles and the streets around it are local streets, so the drains on them would be ours. The state handles its own highways. If it turns out to be something else, we'd pass it along ourselves, you wouldn't have to chase it.
Good. I would appreciate that. Because honestly, I've been calling around about this, and it keeps getting put off.
I'm sorry about that. I don't have an earlier ticket in front of me for this spot, so I'll start a fresh work order and mark the ice as a safety issue.
Please do. And I'd like it noted that it's been days. First, the ice. Second, the water that keeps feeding it. Third, the manhole. That's three problems at one corner.
Three items, one location. I've got it. Now, would you like a call back when a crew has been out? I can put your number on it.
401-555-0188. And that's a landline, so a message on the machine is fine if you're out?

Yes, leave it on the machine. Oh, and one more thing, unrelated but same block. The mailbox down the way got knocked crooked last week. I think a plow or a truck clipped it. I don't know if that's you or the post office.
If a city plow caught it, that can be reported, and I can add a note to this ticket for the crew supervisor. Which house is the mailbox in front of?
Two doors down from me, toward the corner. It's leaning over toward the street now. Not mine, but I noticed.
Okay, I'll note a leaning mailbox two doors down from twenty-four, possible plow contact. The owner can also call us if they want it looked at.
Fine. I'll tell them. So when can I expect somebody? Give me something, even a window.
With ice in an intersection it goes near the top of the list. I'd say someone should look at it today or Monday morning at the latest. The manhole cover may be a separate crew.
Today or Monday. I will be watching for it. If nothing happens by Monday, I will call again, and I'll want the ticket number.

Of course. The ticket number is going to be on the message we leave, but let me give it to you directly once it's entered. Hold on one moment while I save this. [pause] Okay, it's saved. I'll read it slowly.
Go ahead, I have a pen.
It's PW, then four, two, seven, one. I'll repeat that. P, W, four, two, seven, one.
P, W, four, two, seven, one. Got it. Thank you, Lorraine. I just want it fixed before somebody gets hurt.
I understand. Keep clear of that corner if you can, and sand your steps. Have a good afternoon, Ms. Mensah.
You too. Goodbye.
